facts.raw_span: a one-month history of burning sensation and discomfort in her left breast
without fever or systemic symptoms
a 3 × 3 cm palpable mass in the upper quadrant of the left breast
without overlying skin changes
No axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy was noted
Routine blood tests, chest radiograph, and ECG were unremarkable
Breast MRI revealed an ill-defined, deep retroareolar spiculated lesion measuring 3 × 1.5 cm
with an early enhancement peak and associated architectural distortion
no axillary lymphadenopathy or skin thickening was identified
BIRADS IV
breast tissue containing cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells within a dense lymphoid infiltrate
the epithelial cells were positive for cytokeratin AE1/E3 and negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu

concepts.why: The presence of a spiculated lesion with early enhancement peak and architectural distortion on breast MRI, along with the histopathological findings of neoplastic epithelial cells and negative immunohistochemical staining for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu, support the diagnosis of triple-negative breast cancer.
The presence of a palpable mass and a spiculated lesion on breast MRI, along with the histopathological findings of neoplastic epithelial cells, support the diagnosis of invasive ductal carcinoma.

The presence of a dense lymphoid infiltrate and the histopathological findings of neoplastic epithelial cells, along with the negative immunohistochemical staining for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu, support the diagnosis of medullary carcinoma of the breast.

rationales.F07: Spiculated lesion is suspicious for malignancy
rationales.F08: Early enhancement peak and architectural distortion suggest malignancy
rationales.F12: Triple-negative status is characteristic of certain breast cancers

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a dense lymphoid infiltrate and the absence of axillary lymphadenopathy, along with the negative staining for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu, support Medullary carcinoma of the breast as the most specific diagnosis.
